content: RGS20, or Regulator of G-protein signaling 20, is a protein encoded by the RGS20 gene in humans. Regulator of G-protein signaling (RGS) proteins serve as both regulatory and structural components of G-protein-coupled receptor complexes. RGS proteins function as GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs) for the G-alpha subunits of the Gi (e.g., GNAI1, MIM 139310) and Gq (e.g., GNAQ, MIM 600998) classes of G-proteins. These proteins enhance the rate of GTP binding and hydrolysis, thereby expediting the signaling cycle and facilitating both the kinetics and termination of signal transduction. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the RGS20 gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF). RGS20 has been demonstrated to interact with the G-protein subunits GNAO1 and GNAZ.
